subject: economics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a competitive market with many firms, an individual firm is usually a:
options: Price taker that must accept the market price
Price maker that sets its own price
questions.explain: With many rival firms selling similar goods, each firm is a price taker accepting the market price.

questions.q: A surplus in a free market is normally eliminated as:
options: Price falls until demand equals supply
questions.explain: A surplus pushes price down until quantity demanded again equals quantity supplied at equilibrium.

questions.q: A key feature of a monopoly compared with a competitive market is:
options: Free and easy entry for new firms
A single (or dominant) firm able to influence the price
questions.explain: A monopoly is a single dominant seller able to act as a price maker, unlike competitive price takers.

questions.q: A fall in the cost of raw materials used by a firm will:
options: Shift the demand curve to the right
Cause a contraction in supply only
Shift the supply curve to the right
Shift the supply curve to the left
questions.explain: Lower production costs increase supply at every price, shifting the supply curve right.

questions.q: If price is set ABOVE the equilibrium price, the likely result is:
questions.explain: Above equilibrium, supply exceeds demand, creating a surplus that tends to push the price down.

questions.q: A rise in the price of a good, other things equal, causes:
options: A shift of the demand curve to the left
A contraction (decrease) in quantity demanded along the curve
A shift of the supply curve
questions.explain: A price change causes a movement along the demand curve, not a shift; a higher price means a contraction.

questions.q: The 'rationing' function of the price mechanism means that when a good becomes scarce:
options: Its rising price discourages some buyers, sharing out the limited supply
questions.explain: A higher price rations scarce goods by pricing out some buyers so the limited quantity is shared.

questions.q: Market failure occurs when:
options: The free market fails to allocate resources in society's best interests
questions.explain: Market failure is when free markets lead to an inefficient or undesirable allocation of resources.

questions.q: A 'public good' such as street lighting is:
options: Non-excludable and non-rival, so the market under-provides it
Always provided by firms for profit
questions.explain: Public goods are non-excludable and non-rival, so markets fail to supply them and government often does.

questions.q: Which of these would shift the demand curve for tea to the RIGHT?
options: A rise in the price of coffee, a substitute for tea
A rise in the price of milk, a complement
A rise in the price of tea
questions.explain: A dearer substitute (coffee) makes consumers switch to tea, increasing demand and shifting it right.

questions.q: A demerit good, such as cigarettes, is one that:
options: Is over-consumed because consumers ignore its true costs
Is provided free by the government
Has no effect on third parties
questions.explain: Demerit goods are over-consumed because people underestimate their private and external costs.

questions.q: A fall in consumer incomes will, for a normal good, cause:
options: A leftward shift of the demand curve
A movement up the demand curve
A rightward shift of the demand curve
questions.explain: For a normal good, lower incomes reduce demand at every price, shifting the demand curve left.

questions.q: A simultaneous rise in demand and fall in supply will definitely cause:
questions.explain: Higher demand and lower supply both push price upward, so the equilibrium price rises.

questions.q: Which good is most likely to have price INELASTIC demand?
questions.explain: Necessities with few substitutes, such as fuel, tend to have inelastic demand.

questions.q: The price elasticity of supply measures how:
options: Price responds to a change in tax
Demand responds to a change in income
Quantity supplied responds to a change in price
questions.explain: Price elasticity of supply measures the responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price.

questions.q: Demand for a good is described as price INELASTIC when:
options: Quantity demanded changes a lot when price changes
The good has many close substitutes
Demand falls to zero when price rises
Quantity demanded changes only a little when price changes
questions.explain: Inelastic demand means quantity demanded is relatively unresponsive to a change in price.

questions.q: Supply tends to be more price INELASTIC when:
options: Production takes a long time and cannot be increased quickly
There are many ways to switch resources
Firms have lots of spare capacity
questions.explain: Supply is inelastic when output cannot be increased quickly, for example crops that take a season to grow.

questions.q: If demand is price ELASTIC, a firm that lowers its price will see total revenue:
questions.explain: When demand is elastic, the rise in quantity outweighs the lower price, so total revenue rises.

questions.q: In the price mechanism, a sudden rise in demand sends a signal that:
options: Raises price and gives producers an incentive to supply more
questions.explain: Higher demand raises price, signalling and giving producers an incentive to expand output.

questions.q: Luxury goods tend to have demand that is price:
questions.explain: Luxuries are not essential and often have substitutes, so their demand is relatively price elastic.

questions.q: If the equilibrium price of a good rises after demand increases, the price has acted as a:
options: Signal and incentive for producers to supply more
questions.explain: A higher price signals to producers and gives them an incentive to expand output.

questions.q: At the market equilibrium price:
options: There is a shortage of the good
There is a surplus of the good
questions.explain: Equilibrium is where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied and there is no tendency to change.
